subject: Problem with reactive environment in Shiny R

messages.author: aed279f0610b5c0c
messages.subject: Problem with reactive environment in Shiny R
parts:
Hi I am trying to take an input in Shiny, do some calculation on it and then trying to render an output which is the result of the calculation, I am facing the reactivity issue and not being able to solve it. If I use Isolate the calculation does not take the value at all since it is isolate. Below is the code which gives me the reactivity issue;

shinyServer(function(input,output ){
#Checking if Go button has been pressed or not
if (input$goButton == 0){
return()}
#Loan information:
isolate({
loan_amount = as.numeric(input$Loan_amt)
})
ABCD <- loan_amount + 2
output$ABC <- renderText(ABCD)
})


This is the code (given below) which does not give me the updated value of the input

shinyServer(function(input,output ){
#Checking if Go button has been pressed or not
#if (input$goButton == 0){
#return()}
#Loan information:
isolate({
loan_amount = as.numeric(input$Loan_amt)
})
ABCD <- loan_amount + 2
output$ABC <- renderText(ABCD)
})


I have also tried using the Submit button but have not been able to use it successfully. The code is just a sample of the bigger calculation I am trying to do. Any help would be appreciated.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: Problem with reactive environment in Shiny R
parts:
Any code that must be re-run when inputs change must either be in a reactive({...}) or in a renderXXX({...}). The former is for calculations that you want to use in multiple places. Each of your data frames might be one reactive. Reactives can read other reactives too, so any calculations you'll perform should also be in reactive(). Then you can refer to those reactives from your renderXXX.

Seriously though, I'd take another go through the tutorial. If these concepts aren't clear then it will be very frustrating trying to make headway with your app, but once you understand how it's supposed to work it's quite simple and elegant.
